name: Slow Cooker Beef Barbacoa

fit.result: FIT (macros clear the band, but rejected as a duplicate)

dupe_evidence: Duplicates catalog 'slow-cooker-barbacoa-bowl' (Slow Cooker Barbacoa Burrito Bowl). Same dish on 3-of-4 axes and near-identical core: protein = beef-chuck-roast (match), sauce/flavor = chipotle-adobo + lime + apple-cider-vinegar + beef-broth barbacoa (match - catalog items literally include chipotle-adobo, apple-cider-vinegar, limes, beef-broth, onions), method = slow cooker (match). The only difference is the starch/format - the catalog serves the same barbacoa meat over rice + seasoned black beans, this candidate serves it grain-free. Per the rule that a 3-of-4 match survives only if something genuinely distinguishes the PLATE, dropping the rice/beans does not make it a different dinner: it is the identical shredded chipotle barbacoa braise, just re-plated. The candidate's own why-note concedes this is a 'low-carb conversion' of the existing catalog barbacoa bowl - i.e. the near-duplicate that would embarrass the catalog, not a distinct regional take.
borderline_flag: Not treated as borderline. The dish name is 'barbacoa' in both and the meat build is the same; the low-carb re-plating is a format change, not a new dinner. If the decider weighs the low-carb-catalog-gap argument and disagrees, this is the single point of contention - but the shredded barbacoa itself is already in the catalog.
cross_protein_collision: None material for beef. Barbacoa is definitionally beef (cheek/chuck); a pork version would be carnitas (a different dish), so no clean same-dish-different-protein twin is expected in another selector's pool.
unmapped_note: Carries 'chipotles in adobo sauce' as the flagged unmapped ingredient - but the catalog's own barbacoa bowl already maps it as 'chipotle-adobo', reinforcing the duplication rather than adding pricer-lane novelty.
